newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dlr/yen to resume fall if 115.50 crumbles.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dlr/yen to resume fall if 115.50 crumbles.

text.p: Dollar/yen's recovery on Monday was not decisive and analysts said at least one more brush with the downside could ensue if 115.50 gives way.
Another break below 115.50 yen, after several trips under there in recent days, could result in a fast trip to the 113 to 114 yen area before the dollar finds it footing, chartists said.

"I'm watching 115.50 yen as sort of a pivot level," said Thom Worden, global technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "While we're above (115.50) it's okay but the price patterns don't show that we've seen a bottom in dollar/yen.
"We can go lower, the question is how much," he said.
Worden said he expects at least a marginal new low around 113.90 yen if 115.50 yields.
If dollar/yen breaks lower, other analysts said they target 113 before an explosive turnaround.
Rob Kepler, technical analyst at Lehman Brothers, said dollar/yen is consolidating its recent decline in a triangle with parameters of 114.85 and 117.00.
"This little triangle should lead to downside resolution, with a target at 113 (yen). Over 117 though, I would expect a very sharp rally probably up to 119," Kepler said.
Dollar/mark, meanwhile, seems on more solid ground, after escaping from the broad 1.6860 to 1.7090 range which defined its activity most of last week.
The dollar made a hesitant push above the upper level of its recent trading band on Monday, pushing up to 1.7115 marks.
But while the short-term outlook is bullish up to 1.72 marks or so, some analysts said the dollar was a good sell between 1.71 and 1.7150 marks.
"If dollar/mark moves up, I would look for it to peter-out somewhere between 1.71 and 1.7150, then position itself for another attempt to the downside," Worden said.
Key support in dollar/mark lies at 1.6865 and at the May 12 low of 1.6680.
At 1150 GMT/1550 GMT on Monday, the dollar was trading at 1.7105/10 marks, up from 1.7032/37 at the U.S. open. But it was off at 115.97/07 yen, compared to 116.25/30.
